extracted.intended_audience: natural philosophers / experimental scientists and physicians interested in observational experiments and analyses (17th-century readership)
extracted.subtask_description: A procedural analytical checklist for testing and characterising mineral (spring) waters; includes quantitative, qualitative, biological, and physiological assays and observations designed to determine composition, effects, and uses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Checklist: Queries for examining mineral waters
rubrics_metrics.description: A list of explicit queries (Sir William Petty) to be applied when examining mineral waters, covering physical, chemical, biological, and therapeutic properties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the numbered queries below as an experimental/observational protocol when assessing a mineral water's character and possible medicinal uses.

rubrics_metrics.name: How much heavier than brandy?
rubrics_metrics.description: 1. How much heavier than brandy?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine specific gravity relative to brandy (i.e., a comparative density measurement).

rubrics_metrics.name: How much will common water reduce its taste?
rubrics_metrics.description: 2. How much will common water reduce its taste?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess dilution effects on flavour — mix with common water and describe change in taste intensity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantity of salt on evaporation
rubrics_metrics.description: 3. What quantity of salt on evaporation?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaporate a measured volume and weigh/residue to estimate total dissolved salts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solubility of common solutes
rubrics_metrics.description: 4. How much sugar, alum, vitriol, nitre, &c. will dissolve in a pint of it?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test solubility limits for typical salts/compounds to characterise solvent power and ionic content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presence and growth of animalcula
rubrics_metrics.description: 5. Whether any animalcula will breed in it, and in how long time?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe for microbial/infusorial life by leaving samples and recording appearance/time to visible life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support of fish life
rubrics_metrics.description: 6. Whether fish, viz. trouts, eels, &c. will live in it, and how long?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test biological suitability by placing live fish and monitoring survival times and behaviour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect on milk curdling and fermentation
rubrics_metrics.description: 7. Whether it will hinder or promote the curdling of milk and fermentation of liquors, &c.?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use milk and fermentable substrates to see whether the water accelerates or inhibits curdling/fermentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compatibility with soap
rubrics_metrics.description: 8. Whether soap will mingle with it?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test soaping action (lather formation, cleaning) to indicate hardness/alkalinity and mineral content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power as a menstruum / extractor of plant constituents
rubrics_metrics.description: 9. Whether it will extract the dissolvable parts of herbs, roots, seeds, more or less than other water? i.e. whether it be a more powerful menstruum?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare extractions of botanical material (tinctures, infusions) against common water under controlled conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reaction with galls (tannins/inks)
rubrics_metrics.description: 10. How galls will change its colour?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add galls (oak gall tannins) to test for complexation/precipitation and colour changes relevant to tannin chemistry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect on syrups of violets colour
rubrics_metrics.description: 11. How it will change the colour of syrup of violets?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use pH/indicator-sensitive dyes (violet syrup) to detect acid/base or reactive metal effects by colour shifts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differences in dye uptake (cochineal, saffron, violets)
rubrics_metrics.description: 12. How it differs from other waters in receiving the colour of cochineal, saffron, violets, &c.?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare dye uptake/intensity on standard substrates to infer interactions with colouring agents and mordants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooking properties — boiling dry peas
rubrics_metrics.description: 13. How it boils dry pease?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test culinary/thermal effects by cooking standard legumes and observing time-to-cook/texture differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cleaning efficacy — washing hands, boards, linen
rubrics_metrics.description: 14. How it washes hands, boards, linen, &c.?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess cleaning power empirically with standardized soils and laundering procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brewing — extraction of malt
rubrics_metrics.description: 15. How it extracts malt in brewing?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use brewing trials to evaluate saccharification/extraction efficiency and effects on fermentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quenching thirst with meat or otherwise
rubrics_metrics.description: 16. How it quenches thirst with meat or otherwise?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subjective/physiological test of perceived thirst-quenching when consumed with/without food; record effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purgative properties
rubrics_metrics.description: 17. Whether it purges? in what quantity of time and with what symptoms?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administer controlled doses and record laxative/evacuant effects, onset time, and attendant symptoms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effects on urine, sweat, sleep
rubrics_metrics.description: 18. Whether it promote urine, sweat, or sleep, &c.?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor diuresis, perspiration, and sleep after consumption; document dose-response and symptoms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observation: crystalline humour composed of orbicular scaly parts
rubrics_metrics.description: The crystalline body or humour of the eye is composed of many orbicular scaly parts, each beginning from the centre and composed of crystalline globules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cut the crystalline humour with a razor (after drying) and observe the layered scaly structure and globules; record detailed morphology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure: drying and cutting crystalline humour
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow the crystalline humour to dry for 3 days; it becomes very hard and can be cut and observed in parcels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drying makes the structure more easily sectioned and reveals scaly and globular composition; note changes in hardness and breakage pattern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examine the membranous film for thread-like structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine the film or membrane that encloses the crystalline humour for thread-like appearances which may fill unevennesses of the crystal surface and possibly act as a muscle by compressing the crystalline humour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspect under magnification where possible; trace lymphatic-like streaks entering the coat; record presence/absence and functional hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimate scale thickness by hair breadth counting
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimate number of scales and their thickness by measuring axis length and converting inches to hair breadths to infer about 2000 scales in breadth of a hair.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use comparative micrometric reasoning (axis length, hair breadth) to estimate scale counts and thickness when direct measurement tools are lacking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative anatomy across species
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare crystalline bodies across animals (oxen, cows, sheep, hogs, fish, birds): note similarities (scaly composition) and differences (threads' course, globular vs flat shapes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systematically dissect and compare multiple species' eyes, describing thread orientation, globe vs flattened shapes, and changes upon removal of scales.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modeling the crystalline body
rubrics_metrics.description: Represent the crystalline body by winding a small ball with fine cord, fixing with pins and glue, then removing pins to exhibit layered structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use simple physical models to communicate and visualise hypotheses about layered/scale structure for demonstration purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observation method to see thread-like appearances with naked eye
rubrics_metrics.description: Viewing through the rim of a wine glass against a candle, or through a small aperture formed by fingers, produces a thread-like appearance similar to that seen under a microscope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use simple occlusion/aperture tricks and bright point sources to elicit interference-like visual phenomena that reveal fine structures to the unaided eye.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigate vitreous humour behaviour
rubrics_metrics.description: The vitreous humour, though suspected to be a transparent muscle, commonly changes into a watery substance upon examination and is difficult to characterise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note transformation tendencies during dissection and handle gently; report negative observations (failure to detect expected muscular structure) and methodological limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observation of moisture on pupil and role of eyelids
rubrics_metrics.description: There is moisture on the outside of the pupil containing small globules that move when eyelids close; eyelids are necessary to keep the eye moist and prevent rumpling/drying of the surface.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe surface moisture dynamics; experimental scalding of hogs' eyes showed aqueous matter seeping through cornea tunica — document such manipulations and consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation of corneal films reveals tiny vascular streaks
rubrics_metrics.description: Separating thin films of the horny coat reveals interwoven clear transparent streaks, judged to be very small blood vessels lacking visible red globules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Careful mechanical separation may reveal microvessels; interpret redness after rubbing as entry of blood globules into these tiny vessels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative blood globule morphology
rubrics_metrics.description: Blood of oxen, sheep, rabbits shows globules similar in magnitude to human; fishes and birds show flattish oval parts causing redness, suggesting a taxonomic difference in blood particle shape.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare blood smears across taxa to characterise morphology; report species-level differences and avoid overgeneralising from a few specimens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental observation of barometer quicksilver behaviour
rubrics_metrics.description: When quicksilver is very low it visibly breaks and emits small particles; heating the tube expels air; polished iron rusts when immersed in quicksilver, suggesting air mixed with it and particulate 'fretting' affecting barometer readings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe barometer surfaces during descent/ascent; apply heated iron to purge tubes and note chemical effects (e.g., rust) as evidence for dissolved/mixed air and interactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation guideline: liquids nearer their natural state in extreme temperatures
rubrics_metrics.description: Quicksilver and other liquids are nearer their 'own natures' and suffer less violence in very cold and very hot seasons; salts and bodies may crystallise/solidify in both heat and cold — use analogy to interpret humours and health effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ comparative reasoning from materials chemistry (salts/quicksilver) to hypothesise physiological/clinical effects of climate on bodily humours; document analogies and their limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hypothesis for evening blindness — increased viscosity/turbidity of ocular humours
rubrics_metrics.description: Evening blindness may be due to humours becoming thicker and more turbid after sunset, analogous to atmospheric vapours condensing and thickening the near-surface air, thus refracting light and weakening its action on the retina.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame clinical/phenomenological explanations by analogy to environmental physical phenomena; record temporal pattern, seasonality, and testable predictions (e.g., consistency across seasons).
